# Mass-parametrized fiber birth: exact response and a capture obstruction

This note gives a sufficient local descent criterion for a genuinely new variable: positive-dimensional mass born on previously zero-mass integer fibers while all old fibers stay fixed. It includes the pooled covariance derivative and sufficient control of every new candidate. It does not assert that a below-OC body always admits the required geometric birth or capture mixture.

## 1. Geometric hypotheses, stated before taking a derivative

Let d>=1. Let P be a finite old integer base set and let its prescribed compact d-dimensional convex fibers K_z have positive volumes. Write mu for their uniform mixed measure and M=mu(S)>0. Let Q be a finite set of additional integer bases. Choose x_q in R^d and d-dimensional convex bodies D_q, and assume

    sum_(q in Q) |D_q|=1.

Suppose that for every sufficiently small epsilon>=0 there is an ACTUAL compact convex body whose complete sampled fibers are exactly

    K_z                              at z in P,
    x_q+epsilon^(1/d) D_q             at q in Q,          (1)

and no other nonempty integer fibers. At epsilon=0 the second fibers mean singleton points. This is a substantive compatibility hypothesis. Taking a convex hull of independently prescribed fibers does not prove it: every forced intermediate integer fiber must be checked.

The mass is exactly M+epsilon. Let m_q=|D_q| and let

    nu=sum_(q in Q) m_q delta_(q,x_q)                    (2)

be the probability law of limiting birth locations.

A useful sufficient hypothesis for controlling new candidates is that every q is an exposed vertex of conv(P union Q). Then a pure-base halfspace through q isolates its own fiber from every other sampled base. Its points have raw depth at most epsilon m_q, including in the smoothed model in which pure-base caps remain ordinary closed caps. Thus they cannot compete with a positive old maximum for small epsilon.

An alternative is an explicit finite ambient cap cover controlling all new fibers; the seven-fiber interval construction in `candidate dcd790485c83acdc` uses this stronger direct certificate. Without either an exposure/gap argument or such a cover, a calculation at the old sources does not bound the new global maximum.

A precise lattice-global sufficient cover is useful here. Suppose cap groups have inequalities a_ij dot(z-p_i)+u_ij dot(x-y_i)>=0 and positive raw coefficients rho_ij with sum_j rho_ij u_ij=0. Put abar_i=sum_j rho_ij a_ij. If no integer z satisfies ALL strict inequalities abar_i dot(z-p_i)<0, then these caps cover the WHOLE mixed lattice: at each integer z one group has a nonnegative weighted margin, so at least one cap in that group contains every given x. This property is unchanged when the marks y_i move, because their terms cancel. If every individual cap mass is at most B, it bounds every candidate's depth by B, including every born fiber. For outward smoothing, containment still gives the same bound because moving that cap's boundary parallel through a contained candidate can only reduce its smoothed mass.

This cover criterion requires individual cap budgets. A small weighted-average response in a group does not alone bound all its cap masses. Nor is existence of this special integer-source cover asserted. The separate Doignon construction in `candidate 207a0b33a5d3a235` supplies global lattice covers under its own depth-region hypotheses, but its projected contacts need not be integer sources or have the current selected source menus.

If the zero-birth body C_ext contains an actual old convex body C_old with precisely the old sampled set, has the same old fibers, and every q is exposed as above, there is a constant-measure preliminary path

    (1-t)C_old+t C_ext, 0<=t<=1.

It is squeezed between the two bodies, so the old fibers stay fixed. There are no other sampled bases because the entire path lies in C_ext. Each new q-fiber is either empty or the prescribed singleton, since it lies in the singleton q-fiber of C_ext. Whenever it appears, exposure in the sampled base hull isolates it by a pure-base halfspace, giving it zero depth. Thus the mixed measure and the maximum depth remain constant along the preliminary path. Exposure in the sampled hull does not imply that q first enters the real projection at t=1: noninteger projection overhangs can cause earlier entry, which is harmless for this argument. The depth conclusion must not be assumed for arbitrary nonexposed birth locations.

## 2. The actual pooled covariance has a simple first derivative

Use the within-fiber pooled covariance from the pure-width model:

    Sigma=(1/M) sum_z int_(K_z) (x-g_z)(x-g_z)^T dx,

where g_z is the centroid of its OWN fiber. The old Sigma is positive definite. The covariance numerator of a new fiber in (1) is epsilon^(1+2/d) m_q Sigma_(D_q). Its position x_q contributes no additional term because the covariance is centered separately in that fiber. Consequently

    Sigma_epsilon
      =[M Sigma+epsilon^(1+2/d) sum_q m_q Sigma_(D_q)]
          /(M+epsilon)
      =Sigma-(epsilon/M)Sigma+o(epsilon).               (3)

For Gamma(u)=(u^T Sigma u)^(1/2), uniformly on compact nonzero normal sets,

    Gamma_epsilon(u)
      =Gamma(u)[1-epsilon/(2M)]+o(epsilon).             (4)

This would be different for a covariance centered at one global continuous mean. Formula (3) deliberately uses the actual model's within-fiber definition.

## 3. Smoothed cap response

Fix h>0 and the uniform outward kernel

    Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)),
    psi(t)=1_(-1,0)(t).

Let a selected cap through an old source Y_i=(p_i,y_i) have continuous normal u!=0, normalized by Gamma(u)=1. At an old or new physical point w=(z,x), put

    q(w)=[a dot(z-p_i)+u dot(x-y_i)]/h,
    A= int q(w) psi(q(w)) dmu(w) <=0.                  (5)

Its old raw mass is int Psi(q) dmu. The exact first derivative of its old-fiber contribution caused by (4) is A/(2M). Indeed differentiation with respect to Gamma gives -A at Gamma=1, and Gamma'(0)=-1/(2M).

The contribution of the born fibers is

    epsilon int Psi(q(w)) dnu(w)+o(epsilon).           (6)

For a fixed finite cap menu this is uniform in source marks in a fixed neighborhood. It follows by scaling each D_q to its fixed reference body and using the Lipschitz continuity of Psi: its positional error is O(epsilon^(1/d)/h), multiplied by the born mass epsilon. Width and mark perturbations are handled by the same uniform continuity. No open/closed boundary convention is needed at a birth point for fixed h>0.

Thus the full fixed-mark raw derivative is

    b= int Psi(q) dnu + A/(2M).                        (7)

The covariance term has a favorable sign for birth. Omitting it would give a weaker sufficient descent test, but would not be the exact response.

Now take every old globally deepest source, and at each choose a finite actual balanced cap menu satisfying the uniform-envelope hypotheses in `candidate 92662e9a8e20fd35`. Write its response probabilities as theta_ij and set

    W_i(w)=sum_j theta_ij Psi(q_ij(w)),
    Abar_i=sum_j theta_ij A_ij.

The balance is sum_j theta_ij S_ij u_ij=0, with actual smoothed coareas S_ij. Let beta be the old normalized maximum. Combining (7), mark balancing, normalization, and control of ALL new candidates gives

    beta_epsilon
      <=beta+(epsilon/M) max_i
          [int W_i dnu + Abar_i/(2M)-beta]+o(epsilon). (8)

In particular, if the displayed bracket is strictly negative for every old deepest source, the actual new body has strictly smaller smoothed maximum depth for sufficiently small epsilon>0. Menu choice is retained: one may choose any one complete favorable collection for this upper certificate. No separator weights common to every possible menu are asserted.

The cap functions on the unchanged old fibers are C^1 in mark and positive width, since their derivative-kink planes have zero d-dimensional fiber volume and dominated convergence applies. The additional positive-spanning and complete-cover assumptions needed for uniform source envelopes remain explicit; they are not consequences of (3) alone.

## 4. Ordinary depth is a separate limit regime

For h=0, one cannot replace (6) indiscriminately by the closed-cap indicator of the point (q,x_q). If that point lies on the cutting plane, an entire positive-dimensional born fiber can have a nontrivial limiting captured fraction; in d=1 this fraction can also depend on a source displacement of order epsilon.

A clean ordinary version of (8) holds when every birth point has a STRICT nonzero margin for every selected cap and the old cap envelopes have the required threshold regularity. Then each born fiber is eventually wholly captured or wholly missed, uniformly under the relevant O(epsilon) source displacements. The derivative is

    b=nu(H),

there is no width or covariance term, and the bracket in (8) becomes int W_i dnu-beta for the finite indicator menu. This is precisely the strict-margin mechanism in the five-interval augmentation certificate. Ordinary supporting-section singularities or boundary birth points require their own one-sided analysis and are not subsumed by the smoothed calculation.

## 5. A genuine obstruction to automatically favorable birth locations

Consider the sharp product with n=1,d=2: two identical regular triangles T at bases0 and1, with centroid0. Write their barycentric coordinates as lambda_0,lambda_1,lambda_2. The three ordinary minimizing through-centroid directions have margins

    ell_j(x)=lambda_j(x)-1/3,

whose maximum and minimum on T are2/3 and-1/3. At source(0,0), every ordinary active ambient cap must use one of these continuous directions and must receive zero mass from the other triangle: its own mass cannot be less than(4/9)|T|. Its base coefficient a therefore satisfies

    a<=-2/3.

For any integer birth base z<=-1 and any x in T, the margin in EVERY such active cap is at least

    a z+ell_j(x)>=2/3-1/3=1/3>0.                     (9)

This applies to every active menu at that source, not only one selected base tilt. The analogous statement at source1 holds for every birth at z>=2.

Moreover any convex extension preserving both old triangle fibers has all its other real fibers contained in T. For each facet normal of T its support roof is concave and equals the same value at0 and1, so outside that segment it cannot exceed that value. Thus (9) describes ALL geometrically preserving birth locations on the left. The analogous right statement is equally unavoidable.

The same example persists in the positive-width model. For sufficiently small barycentric width w, the exact own-triangle all-angle computation in `candidate 2ab56d1c26a2c4f9` gives only the three canonical active directions, with own raw value

    q_h=|T|(4/9+2w/3+w^2/3).

An active cap at source0 must make the other triangle's smoothed contribution zero, requiring a<=-2/3-w. Every left birth point then has margin at least1/3+w and profile exactly one in EVERY active cap. All right birth points similarly have profile one at source1.

If a preserving birth mixture has left and right total masses L and R, then L+R=1, and its two source capture scores are at least L and R. Their maximum is at least1/2. Here M=2|T|, beta=q_h/M, and the canonical width moment is

    Abar=-(2|T|/3)w(1+w).

Thus the strict test (8) would require both capture scores below

    beta-Abar/(2M)=2/9+w/2+w^2/3,

which is less than1/2, for example when0<w<=1/100. It is impossible. This is a calibrated failure of the proposed sufficient first-order birth test, not a claim about every possible nonlinear or old-fiber-changing extension.

The example is at the sharp ordinary OC value, not below it. It proves that compatibility does not automatically furnish a cheaply captured new fiber, and that one actual source group may capture every available birth on its side in every active cap. A general birth mechanism must use a below-target hypothesis or an additional geometric invariant.

# Mass-parametrized fiber birth: exact response and a capture obstruction

**Exact covariance and cap response for compatible mass birth**

Consider an actual convex birth family with all old positive d-dimensional fibers fixed and new fibers x_q+epsilon^(1/d)D_q satisfying sum_q |D_q|=1. For the pooled within-fiber covariance Sigma, its right derivative at zero is -Sigma/M, where M is the old mixed mass. Fix a positive outward-smoothing width h, a source and a nonvertical cap normal normalized by Gamma(u)=1, and write q(w)=[a.(z-p)+u.(x-y)]/h. With Psi(t)=min(1,max(0,1+t)), psi=1_(-1,0), and A=integral q psi(q) dmu<=0, the raw fixed-cap derivative is integral Psi(q) dnu + A/(2M), where nu is the mass-normalized atomic birth measure. This is the source's positive-width formula; feasibility of the complete birth family is a hypothesis.

Scope limits: Actual simultaneous fiber compatibility, uniform old-source envelopes, and control of every new candidate are assumptions. The corrected preliminary path allows singleton fibers to enter early. For zero smoothing, strict birth margins and separate threshold regularity are required.
